ai-at-work.title: What is sovereign AI — and why it will decide the winners and losers of the AI race
ai-at-work.excerpt: On the four dimensions of real sovereignty, the fifth dimension every chief financial officer is learning about the hard way, and why open source isn’t a preference — it’s the architecture. About this
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Sovereign AI is basically the idea that countries and organizations need to control their own AI infrastructure and data rather than rely on foreign vendors. For digital workplace professionals, this matters because it's going to reshape which tools you can use, where your data lives, and how your company evaluates enterprise AI solutions. Here's the thing though: most organizations are still buying AI like it's just another SaaS subscription, completely blind to the sovereignty question that's about to smack them in the face.

ai-at-work.dwp_take: The EU's European Commission found Meta violated the Digital Services Act by using deceptive interface design to nudge users toward certain choices. This matters because it signals regulators are finally taking dark patterns seriously, which directly affects how we design internal digital workplaces and employee apps. After 30 years watching tech companies get away with manipulative design, it's refreshing to see someone actually call it out instead of just complaining in LinkedIn posts.

ai-at-work.dwp_take: MiniMax Group, a Shanghai-based AI developer, just closed a $2 billion funding round split between equity and convertible bonds. For digital workplace professionals, this signals that open-source AI models are becoming serious infrastructure plays with real money backing them, which means more competition and capability in the AI tools landscape we're all evaluating. The irony is that by the time we finally figure out which AI tool to standardize on, there will be seventeen new well-funded options making the same promises.

ai-at-work.title: Cisco brings enterprise AI infrastructure to the edge: CUBEd Award winner

ai-at-work.dwp_take: Cisco launched Unified Edge, a platform designed to handle AI workloads at the edge of networks rather than relying solely on centralized cloud processing, and it won a 2026 Tech Innovation award for the effort. Here's the thing though: most organizations are still struggling to manage basic cloud infrastructure, so before you get excited about edge AI, make sure you can walk before Cisco sells you the jogging shoes.

digital-culture.title: Companies keep talking about the motherhood penalty. They’re missing the motherhood advantage

digital-culture.title: In a tough job market, don’t make AI your only career coach
digital-culture.excerpt: If you’re like most people, you’re using artificial intelligence in a variety of ways, and you may be relying on its help as a partner in this tough job market. You’re probably even asking AI for care
digital-culture.dwp_take: Fast Company is basically saying AI can help with job hunting but shouldn't be your only career advisor right now. For digital workplace professionals, this matters because we're often the ones implementing these tools and need to understand their actual limitations versus the hype we're selling internally. Here's the truth: an AI trained on yesterday's data giving you career advice in today's market is like asking your GPS from 2015 to navigate a city that just got rebuilt, and pretending it's cutting edge strategy.

The real insight here is that sometimes the oldest trick in the book—a window unit and fan strategy—beats whatever cloud-based thermal management solution some vendor is about to pitch you.
